title: Staged deployment route leak caused eviction loop and promotion block
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a staged model rollout to support a new reranking variant, an unexpected external traffic shift combined with a route-evaluation bug caused a subset of production requests to be persistently routed to the staged variant. This produced a sustained load spike on the variant pool, triggered frequent instance evictions from our autoscaler, and prevented the automated promotion/rollback dance from completing, leaving the rollout in a locked state.
timeline: 2026-03-02T00:42:00Z - Scheduled rollout started: rerank-v2026-03 staged at 10% traffic (routing-policy: split-by-cookie+header)
2026-03-02T01:15:00Z - CDN cache rule change at partner edge caused concentrated burst from a handful of IP ranges (external), increasing traffic routed to the service by ~18%
2026-03-02T01:18:30Z - Routing translator observed header duplication from proxy chain; evaluation chose staged variant for many requests beyond intended split
2026-03-02T01:22:10Z - Variant pool metrics: memory pressure rising; autoscaler began 3 rapid evictions to reclaim headroom
2026-03-02T01:28:45Z - Latency and token-generation time increased; on-call alerted by SLO pager (p95 latency breach)
2026-03-02T01:35:00Z - Automated rollback initiated by rollout controller but failed due to 'variant_lock' state: orchestration flagged an incomplete promotion transaction
2026-03-02T01:40:00Z - Manual mitigation: ops pinned traffic back to baseline model variant and drained staged pool; KV cache warmers and failover route applied
2026-03-02T02:10:00Z - Traffic normalized; automated promotion lock cleared after manual reconcile; incident contained
impact_summary: Customer-facing text-generation p95 latency increased from ~120ms to ~780ms for ~28 minutes. A subset (~9%) of requests saw elevated token generation retries. No data loss; customer requests returned errors <0.1% but end-user latency impact was measurable for high-throughput tenants in EU region.
detection: Pager triggered by SLO alert (latency p95 > 600ms). Dashboard alerts showed eviction spikes and kvcache miss ratio rising. Initial root-cause was not obvious until routing translator logs were inspected and a correlation with CDN partner change was discovered.
root_cause: Intersection of three failures: 1) external traffic redistribution from a partner CDN change temporarily skewed client distribution; 2) routing translator had a header de-duplication edge case where duplicate headers from an upstream proxy favored the staged-split rule, leading to persistent assignment beyond the intended percentage; 3) rollout orchestration assumed idempotent promotion/rollback flows and failed to recover from partial state (variant_lock) when evictions interrupted the controller heartbeat.
mitigation: Immediate manual actions: revert routing rule at edge (partner), apply temporary strict route pin to baseline variant, drain staged variant pool, and run reconciler to clear variant_lock. KV cache warmers and a short-term increase in reserved capacity reduced cold-start pressure. We also paused related rollouts until the translator patch was validated.
long_term_fixes: (ENG) Add strict header canonicalization in routing translator to remove ambiguity from duplicate headers (target: runtime-2.6.1)
(ENG) Make rollout orchestration idempotent and add a recovery path for 'variant_lock' where manual reconcile is not required (target: rollout-controller-1.9)
(SRE) Add autoscaler damping policy for staged-variant pools to avoid rapid evictions from transient spikes (target: autoscaler-0.14)
(PM/Eng) Add pre-rollout canary traffic simulation that models upstream proxy header behavior and partner CDN burst patterns as part of the rollout checklist
(Docs) Update runbook: containment steps for route-leak and instructions to perform safe reconciles without full manual intervention
